checks.finding: design.md Architecture mermaid diagram, Technical Summary and Components table cover (1) component boundaries (fixture matrix, test kinds, golden baseline, schema, loop-inventory/loop-driver/emit-run-record extension points), (2) integration with existing components via explicit extends/compares edges and INV-xxx citations, and (3) technology choices (Bash/PowerShell/JSON/jq; Global Constraints and Assumptions). Interactions are described, not just named.

The dependency edges in the Architecture diagram and Components table are acyclic: fixtures to tests, tests to baseline/schema, and tests to the existing suites and driver. The collector (_loop_trace_emit) and comparator (assert_event_trace) are explicitly separated, with the comparator reading only the finished trace. The REQ-007 manifest dependencies point to upstream epics A1-A6, not back to this package. No cycle found.

The Data Plan has Data Entities (none persisted by this task; future additive schemas are described), Existing Data Affected (none; the 8 loop-inventory entries are unmodified), and Migration Strategy (no migration required, with additive and absent-safe rationale). The compatibility-event-trace/v1, skip-allowlist-manifest/v1 and structural-fixture-corpus/v1 schemas are specified.

The API / Contract Plan lists every new or changed interface with signatures and schemas: assert_capability_applicability, _loop_trace_emit, assert_event_trace, the emit-run-record.sh flags with a four-combination outcome table and capability object shape, capture/promote-golden-baseline.sh, and build_fixture (5-parameter table). There are no HTTP endpoints. Breaking-change status is covered: the no-flag output stays byte-identical and capability-only is a usage error.

The Security Boundaries table names B1 (baseline capture/update), B2 (shared-registry blast radius) and B3 (allowlist manifest integrity), each with an auth/authz mechanism, data classification and OWASP concern. PII: none is handled, and security-spec.md Data Classification confirms this. security-spec.md is consistent with design.md and extends it with B4/B5 and a STRIDE analysis.

SKIP: Feature Type is test-infrastructure specification (no frontend, no browser or UI surface). design.md Layer Specifications records Frontend and UX as N/A, and frontend-spec.md and ux-spec.md are consistent with that.

The Test Strategy has 9 ordered items with concrete artifacts: TEST-018/019/026, tests/install.tests.sh, the golden-trace fixture, the AC-040 static scan and the AC-041 runtime-refusal pair. It states the unit scope and mocking explicitly (no separate unit layer; no new mocks). Integration is covered through the fixture-driven suites. Acceptance is covered by the AC-to-TEST mapping and the AC-026 four-branch disposition. The OQ-004 closure path is stated. No E2E UI path is required for this feature type.

Every component named in Architecture (loop-inventory.json, loop-driver.sh, loop-consistency/loop-escalation suites, emit-run-record.sh, install/uninstall suites, golden-baseline scripts, fixture-matrix builder, trace schema, SKIP manifest) is in the Components table. The existing loop-inventory.tests.sh is an established component cited via INV-002. The Plan sections reference nothing undefined.

The ADR Change Log states no new ADR is needed. Governing decisions are already fixed by ADR-0010, ADR-0016 and ADR-0023, and the precheck adr_inputs is empty. The design introduces no new technology or architectural departure, since it is test-infrastructure only and uses the existing Bash/jq stack. No referenced ADR is missing.
